CHAPTER 01
Overview

Description: The number of users in the e-commerce market in Africa was modeled to stand at 95.47 million users in 2024. Following a continuous upward trend, the number of users has risen by 66.54 million users since 2017. Between 2024 and 2029, the number of
users will rise by 56.98 million users, continuing its consistent upward trajectory. Read more
Note(s): Africa; 2017 to 2029
Source(s): Statista; Statista Market Insights

upward trend. Between 2024 and 2029, the penetration rate will rise by 0.69 percentage points, showing an overall upward trend with periodic ups and downs. Read more
Note(s): Africa; 2017 to 2029
Source(s): Statista; Statista Market Insights

Description: As of 2022, cash was the main payment method used in online retail in Morocco, Kenya, and Egypt, accounting for 58 percent, 35 percent, and 31 percent of the total, respectively. On the other hand, cash was not that prevalent in South Africa, where 43
percent of e-commerce payments occurred by card, and 22 percent by bank transfer. In Nigeria, most digital buyers used card-based payments (36 percent) and bank transfers (29 percent). Read more
Note(s): Africa, Kenya, Morocco, Nigeria, Egypt; 2022
Source(s): PPRO

Description: The share of South African internet users aged 16 to 64 who purchased a product or service online weekly reached nearly 48 percent as of the third quarter of 2022. Furthermore, some 29 percent used an online price comparison service each week.
Conversely, only 5.6 percent used a buy now pay later service. Read more
Note(s): South Africa; Q3 2022; 16-64 years
Source(s): DataReportal; GWI; Hootsuite; We Are Social
